[reviewer finding R3-1, high] A public input fact explicitly tells the IDEA solver that the target work's distinctive method phrasing is 'in-distribution'. That is a fragment of the method's distinctive name, which scope section 3 forbids on every public surface. It is also a direct hint at the target contribution: query the fitted model only at in-distribution inputs. This is exactly the idea the IDEA task asks the solver to discover. The leak was introduced by this round's rewording, so it is a regression. The fact-ID visibility label (allowed_stages LIT/IDEA, discloses_target_contribution=false) does not match the content.
Required repair: Rewrite the public F-MS-01 to state only the version list, the dates and that an identity/disclosure scan of the supplied background HTML found no reference to the target work. Do not list the search terms, the method phrase, author surnames or hit details. Move the detailed search record (terms searched, hits) to a private fact (e.g. F-MS-02, allowed_stages=[]). Re-scan every public fact and asset for the phrase and its variants ('in-distribution', 'in distribution'). Update the hashes and the public-surface record.

[reviewer finding R3-2, medium] R6 and F-BG-28 report that in the [Oka24] v1 simulations counterfactual attribution outperformed TOCA. They omit the source's stated regime: the methods were evaluated 'with known structural assignments' (Fig. 1 and Fig. 3 captions), i.e. with the true SCM rather than a fitted one. R8 then sets this result against Har24's fitted-SCM failure under the heading that fitted-model-based attributions can be unreliable, as if both were fitted-model evidence. The IDEA question is precisely about fix assessment with an SCM fitted on normal data. Losing this condition misrepresents the closest prior evidence. It could steer solvers to infer that counterfactuals beat interventional analysis even with fitted models, and it affects how judges read boundary hypotheses. The [Oka24] PetShop statement (S5.p9; TOCA 'relies heavily ... on the SCM', with the SCM learned from data) is a different regime and is correctly kept separate.
Required repair: In R6 (Oka24 simulation bullet), add that the simulations evaluated the methods with known structural assignments (the true generating SCM, Fig. 1 caption). Make the same change in F-BG-28, and add locator S5.F1 caption / A2.F3 caption. In R8, rephrase the comparison so that the [Oka24] simulation ranking is attributed to the known-SCM setting and is not presented as fitted-model evidence. Keep the result qualitative, with no numbers and no experiment-scale details (50 nodes, 1000 samples, perturbation grid). Recompute the asset sha256 values.

[reviewer finding R3-3, low] A case-insensitive search for the target author surnames finds 'Sharma' in bg016 (DoWhy citations to A. Sharma), as well as 'Srivastava' in bg014/bg018. The record that the only hits were in bg014/bg018 is therefore inaccurate. These hits cite DoWhy/other works, not the target contribution, so there is no disclosure. However, the provenance statement is wrong, and its current form sits on a public surface.
Required repair: When moving the search record to a private fact (R3-1), state it accurately. List the surname hits in bg014 and bg018 (Srivastava) and bg016 (A. Sharma, DoWhy citations), and note that none refers to the target work.
